title: Extreme-ultraviolet spectroscopy using quantum logic: a feasibility study for singly-ionized helium
authors: A. Martínez de Velasco, V. P. J. Barbé, E. L. Gründeman, A. Díaz Calderon, M. Collombon, J. J. Krauth, C. F. Roth, M. Favier, R. Taieb, T. E. Mehlstäubler, P. O. Schmidt, L. S. Dreissen, K. S. E. Eikema
abstract: Extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) spectroscopy represents an important new direction in precision physics, with potential applications ranging from the metrology of fundamental constants to tests of physics beyond the Standard Model. However, the application of quantum control methods for precision spectroscopy remains an open challenge in the XUV range. Here we present a novel quantum logic (QL) spectroscopy method for precision spectroscopy of weak XUV transitions, and numerically validate its feasibility for the $1S-2S$ transition at 40.81\,eV in singly-ionized helium (He$^{+}$). We propose a scheme based on a single He$^{+}$ ion co-trapped with a Be$^{+}$ ion in a Paul trap, and He$^{+}$ excitation with pairs of frequency-comb (FC) laser pulses upconverted to the XUV via High-Harmonic Generation (HHG). We investigate a nondestructive QL scheme to detect $1S-2S$ excitation, and compare its performance with a destructive readout based on state-selective ionization. Phase coherence of the XUV light is modelled and an optical cavity is used to filter the FC pulses prior to HHG. We model the motional excitation dynamics of trapped ions outside the Lamb-Dicke regime, and numerically validate a scheme we proposed in \cite{Grundeman} to cancel the first-order Doppler broadening and the recoil shift by synchronizing the ion's secular period with the time delay between the two excitation pulses. We show that precision spectroscopy of the $1S-2S$ transition in He$^{+}$ at the 10 kHz level is feasible, for improved tests of quantum electrodynamics (QED), a measurement of the Rydberg constant $R_{\infty}$ independent of hydrogen measurements, or an improved determination of the alpha particle and helion charge radii. The proposed method may also be applied to XUV spectroscopy of other ions outside the Lamb-Dicke regime.
summary: This paper presents a feasibility study for using Quantum Logic spectroscopy combined with Ramsey-Comb techniques to measure the $1S-2S$ transition in $	ext{He}^+$ in the XUV range. By addressing technical challenges like Doppler broadening and phase noise, the authors demonstrate that high precision spectroscopy, crucial for testing QED, is achievable with trapped ions and high-harmonic generation sources.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of performing high-precision spectroscopy in the Extreme-Ultraviolet (XUV) range, specifically targeting the $1S-2S$ transition in singly-ionized helium ($	ext{He}^+$).
main_result: The authors show that achieving spectroscopic precision at the $10 	ext{ kHz}$ level is feasible using their proposed method, enabling improved tests of Quantum Electrodynamics (QED) or precise measurements of fundamental constants.
method: They propose a novel Quantum Logic (QL) spectroscopy method combined with Ramsey-Comb Spectroscopy (RCS) to interrogate the weak XUV transition.
model_or_system: The experiment uses a single $	ext{He}^+$ ion co-trapped with a $	ext{Be}^+$ ion in a Paul trap. Excitation is achieved by upconverting frequency-comb (FC) laser pulses to the XUV via High-Harmonic Generation (HHG).
key_observables: The primary observable is the population oscillation of the $2S$ state, measured via a nondestructive QL readout scheme.
important_parameters: The target transition is the $1S-2S$ transition at $40.81 	ext{ eV}$; the required precision is $10^{-12}$ fractional uncertainty.
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include using an optical cavity to filter FC pulses for phase coherence and modeling motional dynamics outside the Lamb-Dicke regime.
figures_summary: Figure 1 depicts the Ramsey-comb spectroscopy setup using two-color NIR and XUV pulses, while Figure 2 shows simulated RCS fringes illustrating the population dynamics of the $2S$ state.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the need for XUV spectroscopy, proposes the QL-RCS scheme for $	ext{He}^+$, details the technical solutions for Doppler/recoil cancellation and phase coherence, and concludes with the feasibility demonstration for high-precision measurements.
why_interesting: This work represents a state-of-the-art integration of several advanced quantum optics techniques—trapped ions, XUV combs, and quantum control—to push the boundaries of fundamental constant measurements.
